title: Spanish Arrival on Panay
description: Captain Diego de Legazpi and Spanish expeditions navigate the Panay River in search of fertile grounds and sustenance, establishing one of the earliest Spanish settlements in Western Visayas.

title: Establishment of the Parish of Capiz
description: The settlement of Capiz is canonically established as an independent parish under the patronage of the Immaculate Conception, giving birth to the historic Metropolitan Cathedral.

title: Capital of Capiz Province
description: Capiz town is designated the provincial capital and politico-military center of the province, consolidating regional trade and coastal defense along the Sibuyan Sea.

title: The Dakong Lingganay
description: The colossal Santa Monica Church bell is cast using 70 sacks of coins donated by local citizens. Weighing over 10.4 metric tons, it remains the largest Catholic church bell in Asia and a symbol of collective Capiznon devotion.

title: Birth of Manuel A. Roxas
description: On January 1, Manuel Acuña Roxas is born in Capiz. He rose through provincial leadership to become the first President of the independent Third Republic of the Philippines.

title: Liberation of Capiz
description: Capiznon revolutionary forces led by General Esteban Contreras and local patriots defeat Spanish forces, proudly hoisting the Philippine flag in the plaza of Capiz.

title: The Historic Roxas City Bridge
description: Construction of the iconic concrete arched bridge spanning the scenic Panay River is completed, seamlessly linking the city's commercial and civic quarters.

title: Liberation & Guerrilla Heroism
description: The 6th Military District guerillas and Allied forces liberate Capiz from Japanese wartime occupation after years of underground mountain resistance.

title: Charter of Roxas City
description: On April 11, 1951, President Elpidio Quirino signs Republic Act No. 603, officially creating Roxas City in honor of its greatest statesman, President Manuel A. Roxas.

title: Seafood Capital Proclamation
description: Roxas City earns nationwide recognition as the 'Seafood Capital of the Philippines', celebrated for its rich marine biodiversity, oysters, blue crabs, and the resurgence of the prized Diwal clam.

title: Resilience in the Wake of Yolanda
description: Following Super Typhoon Yolanda (Haiyan), the citizens of Roxas demonstrate profound community resilience (Pag-ulikid), pioneering nationwide models of climate-adapted coastal reconstruction.

title: Civic Tech & Sustainable Growth
description: Roxas City expands digital public governance, mangrove rehabilitation in Palina, and participatory democracy through civic-tech initiatives and community-driven portals.
